_**User (2026-10-08 03:38:59Z)**_

Review target: `76`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

219	+		return false, err
220	+	}
221	+	return !has, nil
222	+}
223	+
224	+// IsTwoFactorBlockedByAnyOrg reports whether u is a member of, or a collaborator on a repository of, an
225	+// organization whose two-factor policy blocks them
226	+func IsTwoFactorBlockedByAnyOrg(ctx context.Context, u *user_model.User) (bool, error) {
227	+	if lacks, err := lacksPolicyTwoFactor(ctx, u); err != nil || !lacks {
228	+		return false, err
229	+	}
230	+	isMember, err := db.GetEngine(ctx).
231	+		Where(builder.Eq{"uid": u.ID}).
232	+		And(builder.In("org_id", user_model.RequireTwoFactorOrgIDsBuilder())).
233	+		Exist(new(OrgUser))
234	+	if err != nil || isMember {
235	+		return isMember, err
236	+	}
237	+	return db.GetEngine(ctx).Table("collaboration").
238	+		Join("INNER", "repository", "`repository`.id = `collaboration`.repo_id").
239	+		Where(builder.Eq{"`collaboration`.user_id": u.ID}).
240	+		And(builder.In("`repository`.owner_id", user_model.RequireTwoFactorOrgIDsBuilder())).
241	+		Exist()
242	+}
243	+
244	+// notTwoFactorBlockedOrgCond is the SQL twin of IsTwoFactorBlocked for a query over orgIDCol
245	+func notTwoFactorBlockedOrgCond(orgIDCol string, userID int64) builder.Cond {
246	+	return builder.Or(
247	+		user_model.TwoFactorPolicyExemptCond(userID),
248	+		builder.NotIn(orgIDCol, user_model.RequireTwoFactorOrgIDsBuilder()),
249	+	)
250	+}
251	+
252	+// CountOrgMembersWithoutTwoFactor counts the organization's members enrolled in neither TOTP nor WebAuthn.
253	+// Site administrators are excluded because the policy never blocks them.
254	+func CountOrgMembersWithoutTwoFactor(ctx context.Context, orgID int64) (int64, error) {
255	+	return db.GetEngine(ctx).
256	+		Join("INNER", "user", "`user`.id = `org_user`.uid").
257	+		Where(builder.Eq{"`org_user`.org_id": orgID}).
258	+		And(builder.Eq{"`user`.is_admin": false}).
259	+		And(builder.Not{user_model.HasTwoFactorCond("`org_user`.uid")}).
260	+		Count(new(OrgUser))
261	+}
262	+
263	+// CountOrgOutsideCollaboratorsWithoutTwoFactor counts the non-members who collaborate on any of the
264	+// organization's repositories and are enrolled in neither TOTP nor WebAuthn.
265	+func CountOrgOutsideCollaboratorsWithoutTwoFactor(ctx context.Context, orgID int64) (int64, error) {
266	+	return db.GetEngine(ctx).Table("collaboration").
267	+		Join("INNER", "repository", "`repository`.id = `collaboration`.repo_id").
268	+		Where(builder.Eq{"`repository`.owner_id": orgID}).
269	+		And(builder.NotIn("`collaboration`.user_id", builder.Select("uid").From("org_user").Where(builder.Eq{"org_id": orgID}))).
270	+		And(builder.Not{user_model.HasTwoFactorCond("`collaboration`.user_id")}).
271	+		Distinct("`collaboration`.user_id").
272	+		Count()
273	+}

488	index 0000000000..243efa8f95
489	--- /dev/null
490	+++ b/models/user/two_factor_policy.go
491	@@ -0,0 +1,33 @@
492	+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
493	+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
494	+
495	+package user
496	+
497	+import "xorm.io/builder"
498	+
499	+// RequireTwoFactorOrgIDsBuilder selects the IDs of the organizations that require two-factor authentication.
500	+func RequireTwoFactorOrgIDsBuilder() *builder.Builder {
501	+	return builder.Select("`user`.id").From("`user`").Where(builder.Eq{"`user`.require_two_factor": true})
502	+}
503	+
504	+// HasTwoFactorCond matches rows whose userIDCol (e.g. "`org_user`.uid") is a user enrolled in TOTP or WebAuthn.
505	+func HasTwoFactorCond(userIDCol string) builder.Cond {
506	+	return builder.Or(
507	+		builder.In(userIDCol, builder.Select("uid").From("two_factor")),
508	+		builder.In(userIDCol, builder.Select("user_id").From("webauthn_credential")),
509	+	)
510	+}
511	+
512	+// TwoFactorPolicyExemptCond is the SQL twin of organization.IsTwoFactorBlocked: it is true when no
513	+// organization's two-factor policy can block the user, because they are a site admin, not a person
514	+// (an organization pushing through a deploy key) or enrolled in TOTP or WebAuthn.
515	+func TwoFactorPolicyExemptCond(userID int64) builder.Cond {
516	+	return builder.Or(
517	+		builder.Exists(builder.Select("`user`.id").From("`user`").Where(builder.Eq{"`user`.id": userID}.And(builder.Or(
518	+			builder.Eq{"`user`.is_admin": true},
519	+			builder.NotIn("`user`.type", UserTypeIndividual, UserTypeBot),
520	+		)))),
521	+		builder.Exists(builder.Select("id").From("two_factor").Where(builder.Eq{"uid": userID})),
522	+		builder.Exists(builder.Select("id").From("webauthn_credential").Where(builder.Eq{"user_id": userID})),
523	+	)
524	+}

555	+// denyTwoFactorBlocked responds 403 and returns true when the org requires a 2FA that the doer, a member, lacks
556	+func denyTwoFactorBlocked(ctx *context.APIContext, orgID int64) bool {
557	+	org := ctx.Org.Organization
558	+	if org == nil || org.ID != orgID {
559	+		var err error
560	+		if org, err = organization.GetOrgByID(ctx, orgID); err != nil {
561	+			ctx.APIErrorInternal(err)
562	+			return true
563	+		}
564	+	}
565	+	blocked, err := org.IsTwoFactorBlocked(ctx, ctx.Doer)
566	+	if err != nil {
567	+		ctx.APIErrorInternal(err)
568	+		return true
569	+	}
570	+	if blocked {
571	+		ctx.APIError(http.StatusForbidden, "This organization requires two-factor authentication; enable it on your account to regain access")
572	+	}
573	+	return blocked
574	+}

// GetDoerRepoPermission returns the repository permission for the current actor,
// dispatching to GetActionsUserRepoPermission when the actor is an Actions token user.
func GetDoerRepoPermission(ctx context.Context, repo *repo_model.Repository, user *user_model.User) (Permission, error) {
	if taskID, ok := user_model.GetActionsUserTaskID(user); ok {
		return GetActionsUserRepoPermission(ctx, repo, user, taskID)
	}
	return GetIndividualUserRepoPermission(ctx, repo, user)
}

// GetIndividualUserRepoPermission returns the permissions for an explicit user identity.
// In most request paths, callers should use GetDoerRepoPermission instead.
// Unlike GetDoerRepoPermission, this helper does not resolve Actions task users.
func GetIndividualUserRepoPermission(ctx context.Context, repo *repo_model.Repository, user *user_model.User) (perm Permission, err error) {
	defer func() {
		if err == nil {
			finalProcessRepoUnitPermission(user, &perm)
		}
		log.Trace("Permission Loaded for user %-v in repo %-v, permissions: %-+v", user, repo, perm)
	}()

	if err = repo.LoadUnits(ctx); err != nil {
		return perm, err
	}
	perm.units = repo.Units

	// anonymous user visit private repo.
	if user == nil && repo.IsPrivate {
		perm.AccessMode = perm_model.AccessModeNone
		return perm, nil
	}

	var isCollaborator bool
	if user != nil {
		isCollaborator, err = repo_model.IsCollaborator(ctx, repo.ID, user.ID)
		if err != nil {
			return perm, err
		}
	}

	if err = repo.LoadOwner(ctx); err != nil {
		return perm, err
	}

	// A member or collaborator without the 2FA the owner org requires gets only what a signed-in non-member gets
	if blocked, err := organization.OrgFromUser(repo.Owner).IsTwoFactorBlocked(ctx, user); err != nil {
		return perm, err
	} else if blocked {
		if organization.HasOrgOrUserVisibleToNonMember(repo.Owner, user) {
			perm.AccessMode = publicAccessMode(user, repo)
		}
		return perm, nil
	}

	// Prevent strangers from checking out public repo of private organization/users
	// Allow user if they are a collaborator of a repo within a private user or a private organization but not a member of the organization itself
	// TODO: rename it to "IsOwnerVisibleToDoer"
	if !organization.HasOrgOrUserVisible(ctx, repo.Owner, user) && !isCollaborator {
		perm.AccessMode = perm_model.AccessModeNone
		return perm, nil
	}

	// anonymous visit public repo
	if user == nil {
		perm.AccessMode = perm_model.AccessModeRead
		return perm, nil
	}

	// Admin or the owner has super access to the repository
	if user.IsAdmin || user.ID == repo.OwnerID {
		perm.AccessMode = perm_model.AccessModeOwner
		return perm, nil
	}

	// plain user TODO: this check should be replaced, only need to check collaborator access mode
	perm.AccessMode, err = accessLevel(ctx, user, repo)
	if err != nil {
		return perm, err
	}

	if !repo.Owner.IsOrganization() {
		return perm, nil
	}

	// now: the owner is visible to doer, if the repo is public, then the min access mode is read
	minAccessMode := util.Iif(!repo.IsPrivate && !user.IsRestricted, perm_model.AccessModeRead, perm_model.AccessModeNone)
	perm.AccessMode = max(perm.AccessMode, minAccessMode)

// reqOrgOwnership user should be an organization owner, or a site admin
func reqOrgOwnership() func(ctx *context.APIContext) {
	return func(ctx *context.APIContext) {
		if ctx.IsUserSiteAdmin() {
			return
		}

		var orgID int64
		if ctx.Org.Organization != nil {
			orgID = ctx.Org.Organization.ID
		} else if ctx.Org.Team != nil {
			orgID = ctx.Org.Team.OrgID
		} else {
			setting.PanicInDevOrTesting("reqOrgOwnership: unprepared context")
			ctx.APIErrorInternal(errors.New("reqOrgOwnership: unprepared context"))
			return
		}

		isOwner, err := organization.IsOrganizationOwner(ctx, orgID, ctx.Doer.ID)
		if err != nil {
			ctx.APIErrorInternal(err)
			return
		} else if !isOwner {
			if ctx.Org.Organization != nil {
				ctx.APIError(http.StatusForbidden, "Must be an organization owner")
			} else {
				ctx.APIErrorNotFound()
			}
			return
		}
		denyTwoFactorBlocked(ctx, orgID)
	}
}

// issuePullAccessibleRepoCond userID must not be zero, this condition require join repository table
func issuePullAccessibleRepoCond(repoIDstr string, userID int64, owner *user_model.User, team *organization.Team, isPull bool) builder.Cond {
	cond := builder.NewCond()
	unitType := unit.TypeIssues
	if isPull {
		unitType = unit.TypePullRequests
	}
	if owner != nil && owner.IsOrganization() {
		if team != nil {
			cond = cond.And(teamUnitsRepoCond(repoIDstr, userID, owner.ID, team.ID, unitType)) // special team member repos
		} else {
			cond = cond.And(
				builder.Or(
					repo_model.UserOrgUnitRepoCond(repoIDstr, userID, owner.ID, unitType), // team member repos
					repo_model.UserOrgPublicUnitRepoCond(userID, owner.ID),                // user org public non-member repos, TODO: check repo has issues
				),
			)
		}
	} else {
		cond = cond.And(
			builder.Or(
				repo_model.UserOwnedRepoCond(userID),                          // owned repos
				repo_model.UserAccessRepoCond(repoIDstr, userID),              // user can access repo in a unit independent way
				repo_model.UserAssignedRepoCond(repoIDstr, userID),            // user has been assigned accessible public repos
				repo_model.UserMentionedRepoCond(repoIDstr, userID),           // user has been mentioned accessible public repos
				repo_model.UserCreateIssueRepoCond(repoIDstr, userID, isPull), // user has created issue/pr accessible public repos
			),
		)
	}
	return cond
}

func applyAssigneeCondition(sess db.Session, assigneeID string) {
	// old logic: 0 is also treated as "not filtering assignee", because the "assignee" was read as FormInt64
	if assigneeID == "(none)" {
		sess.Where("issue.id NOT IN (SELECT issue_id FROM issue_assignees)")
	} else if assigneeID == "(any)" {
		sess.Where("issue.id IN (SELECT issue_id FROM issue_assignees)")
	} else if assigneeIDInt64, _ := strconv.ParseInt(assigneeID, 10, 64); assigneeIDInt64 > 0 {
		sess.Join("INNER", "issue_assignees", "issue.id = issue_assignees.issue_id").
			And("issue_assignees.assignee_id = ?", assigneeIDInt64)
	}
}
// NotTwoFactorBlockedRepoCond stops a membership-derived condition from matching the repos of organizations
// whose two-factor policy blocks the user; it is the SQL twin of the check in access.GetIndividualUserRepoPermission
func NotTwoFactorBlockedRepoCond(idStr string, userID int64) builder.Cond {
	return builder.Or(
		user_model.TwoFactorPolicyExemptCond(userID),
		builder.NotIn(idStr, builder.Select("id").From("repository").Where(builder.In("owner_id", user_model.RequireTwoFactorOrgIDsBuilder()))),
	)
}

// UserAssignedRepoCond return user as assignee repositories list
func UserAssignedRepoCond(id string, userID int64) builder.Cond {
	return builder.And(
		builder.Eq{
			"repository.is_private": false,
		},
		builder.In(id,
			builder.Select("issue.repo_id").From("issue_assignees").
				InnerJoin("issue", "issue.id = issue_assignees.issue_id").
				Where(builder.Eq{
					"issue_assignees.assignee_id": userID,
				}),
		),

### Code Review — @vvchopra

**Checked:** Read the full diff against `main` (Go replay and queries, route and permissions, Vue
component, utils, locale strings, tests) and traced the replay by hand for items that leave the
milestone, closed milestones and toggle round-trips. I have not yet run the tests or the page
locally. <!-- TODO before posting: run `go test ./models/issues/ ./services/issue/` and
`pnpm exec vitest RepoMilestoneBurndown`, open a milestone page, and update this line -->

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | 7 | All ten ACs are addressed. Edge cases found: (R1) a closed milestone's chart runs past its close date when an item that already left it is closed later; (R2) toggling "Include pull requests" twice quickly can show data that doesn't match the checkbox; (R3) a viewer who can read PRs but not issues sees "no issues or pull requests yet" by default. |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | 8 | Strong: a pure calculation with 23 table cases, permission tests confirmed to fail without the check, vitest and e2e. Missing a case for R1 (item leaves, then closes after the milestone closes) and a far-off projection (O2). |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | 8 | Clean, well commented, with tight queries. Optional: skip zero-count deltas in `replayMilestoneItem` (fixes R1 at the root), and count `Added`/`Removed` from `Changes` instead of tracking both. |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | 9 | Very thorough. The PR maps every AC, and the deliberate departures from the issue are explained. Course docs and their guide twins are updated. |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | 8 | The AI section says what the AI did and what the author decided, including catching three missed ACs. It doesn't say which results the author checked personally, apart from approving commits. |
| Overall — merge as-is? | 7 | Merge after R1–R3. The optional items can follow later. |

**Required**

- **R1** `services/issue/milestone_burndown.go` `replayMilestoneItem`: a close or reopen while the
  item is outside the milestone still produces a (zero-count) delta. `CalcMilestoneBurndown` then
  does `end = max(ClosedDateUnix, deltas[last].at)`, so a milestone closed on Mar 1 whose former
  item closed on Jun 1 charts flat through June. Only append a delta when `remaining != 0 || scope != 0`.
  That also stops `lastAt` from picking up unrelated events.
- **R2** `RepoMilestoneBurndown.vue` `fetchBurndown`: overlapping requests aren't sequenced, so a
  slower `include_pulls=1` response can land after the user unticks the box. Drop superseded
  responses (request counter or `AbortController`).
- **R3** `routers/web/repo/milestone.go` `MilestoneBurndownData`: if the viewer can't read issues
  (e.g. the issues unit is off), both kinds are off by default and the chart says the milestone is
  empty. Default to pull requests in that case, or pre-tick the box.

**Optional**

- **O1** If a refetch fails, the header keeps the previous summary next to the "failed" title.
  Clear `burndown` or hide the summary on error.
- **O2** The projection isn't capped like the due date (`burndownHorizonDays`). A slow burn
  (e.g. 100 left, 1 closed in 14 days → about 4 years) stretches the axis and squashes the history.
- **O3** `projected_on_time` / `projected_late` read "1 days" when the difference is one day.
- **O4** An issue transferred to another repo disappears from every past day, because the queries
  filter on its current `repo_id`. Probably fine to leave as a known limitation, but worth a line
  in the PR.

```text
feat(org): require two-factor authentication for an organization's members and collaborators
Jack-Donohue
Closes #35

## What changed

Organization owners get a **Require two-factor authentication** checkbox in the organization's settings. While it is on, a member or outside collaborator who has neither TOTP nor a passkey is treated exactly as a signed-in **non-member** of the organization until they enrol. Nothing is deleted, so enrolling gives them everything back on the next request.

- **Policy flag:** a `require_two_factor` column on `user` (organizations are `user` rows), next to `repo_admin_change_team_access`. Migration v344 adds it with an index.
- **One check:** `Organization.IsTwoFactorBlocked(ctx, user)` in the new `models/organization/org_two_factor.go`.
  - It exempts site admins and non-person identities. A deploy-key push runs as the organization itself, which never has 2FA.
  - The 2FA lookup is cached per request (`cachegroup.UserHasTwoFactor`), as the issue asks.
- **Enforced fail-closed in the shared layer**, so every access path inherits it:
  - `GetIndividualUserRepoPermission` gives a blocked user the non-member permission. It reuses the existing "stranger" rules, now factored out as `publicAccessMode` and `HasOrgOrUserVisibleToNonMember`. This one place covers web, API, git over HTTP and SSH, the pre-receive hook, LFS, notifications, mail and maintainer edits. `IsUserRepoAdmin` and `IsUserRealRepoAdmin` get the same check.
  - SQL twin: every per-user, membership-derived condition in `models/repo/repo_list.go`, plus the team filter in `issue_search.go`, gets `NotTwoFactorBlockedRepoCond`. This covers repository lists and search, "my repositories", the dashboard, feeds and the issue search.
  - Organization level:
    - `HasOrgOrUserVisible` (a blocked member can't see a private org);
    - `Organization.UnitPermission` (org projects and packages units);
    - `CanCreateOrgRepo` / `GetOrgsCanCreateRepoByUserID` (create, fork, migrate and transfer into the org);
    - `OrgAssignment` (web: member, owner and team flags cleared);
    - the API's owner, member and team guards (403 with "This organization requires two-factor authentication…");
    - packages' `determineAccessMode`, API migrate, the API member list and team mentions.
- **Opt-out for bookkeeping:** code that *deletes or changes rows* because a user's access looks gone runs its check inside `organization.IgnoreTwoFactorPolicy(ctx)`. Otherwise a temporarily blocked user would permanently lose those rows. The affected code:
  - re-checking assignees and watches after access changes;
  - the team-repo clean-up;
  - the transfer "give the new owner read access" step;
  - the branch-protection allowlist save;
  - recounting official reviews.
- **Settings:**
  - the checkbox is a plain `bool` form field, so unticking it is saved;
  - an owner without 2FA who is not a site admin can't turn the policy on;
  - the page shows how many members and outside collaborators lack 2FA.
- **Compliance view:**
  - for owners, the Members page shows a count and a "No access until 2FA is set up" label on each member without 2FA;
  - a repository's Collaborators settings page shows the same label.
- **Banner:** a blocked user sees "An organization you belong to requires two-factor authentication…" on every page except the enrolment pages.
  - It is computed lazily in `PageGlobalData`, so it costs nothing on pages that don't render it.
  - Removing a TOTP device or the last passkey now refreshes the session's "has 2FA" flag. Before this, the flag stayed `true` until the next sign-in, which also affected the site-wide `TWO_FACTOR_AUTH = enforced` setting.
- **Context docs:** `.claude-students/docs/models-user-org-perm.md` and `docs/testing.md`, and their guides, record:
  - the policy and its opt-out rule;
  - this fork's permission function names;
  - that `loginUser` can't get past TOTP.

## Why

An organization had no way to require 2FA, so one member's reused password was enough to read its private code, packages and secrets. The site-wide `TWO_FACTOR_AUTH = enforced` setting is only checked in the web and API repository middleware. Git over HTTP and SSH, LFS, packages and every listing ignore it, which is exactly the "scattered checks leave gaps" problem the issue warns about. That is why this PR enforces the policy in the shared permission layer instead.

| AC | How it is met |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | The checkbox saves on and off. The off case is tested by posting without the field. |
| AC2 | `SettingsPost` refuses to turn it on for an owner without 2FA and shows an error. |
| AC3 | `GetIndividualUserRepoPermission` returns the non-member permission: 404 on private repositories through web, API, git HTTP and SSH; read-only on public ones. |
| AC4 | `OrgAssignment` gives 404 on member-only pages, and the API guards give 403 with the message. Repository creation and package uploads are refused. |
| AC5 | The SQL conditions drop the org's private repositories from lists, search, the dashboard and feeds. `CheckRepoUnitUser` stops notifications and mail. |
| AC6 | No row is deleted. Bookkeeping code uses `IgnoreTwoFactorPolicy`. Enrolling restores access on the next request. |
| AC7 | The banner, hidden on the enrolment pages. |
| AC8 | Counts on the Settings page; count and labels on the Members page; labels on the Collaborators page. |
| AC9 | Site admins, deploy keys (the organization as doer) and Actions users are exempt. |
| AC10 | The column defaults to false, and the full regression runs below pass unchanged. |

## How it was tested

The API-path integration test was written first and failed before any enforcement existed: 404 expected, 200 returned, and so on.

| Test | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| `models/migrations/v1_27/v344_test.go` | The migration adds `require_two_factor`, false for an individual and an organization. |
| `models/organization/org_two_factor_test.go` | `IsTwoFactorBlocked` for a member without 2FA, a site admin, TOTP, WebAuthn, the organization itself, ghost and anonymous users, and `IgnoreTwoFactorPolicy`. Also: both compliance counts; `CanCreateOrgRepo` and `GetOrgsCanCreateRepoByUserID`; `IsTwoFactorBlockedByAnyOrg` for a member and an outside collaborator; private-org visibility. |
| `models/perm/access/repo_permission_two_factor_test.go` | A blocked member and owner have no access to a private repository. A blocked collaborator gets **exactly** a stranger's permission on a public one, including the restricted-user case. `CheckRepoUnitUser` is false. Admins and deploy keys are unaffected, the opt-out sees real access, the repo-admin checks are false, and enrolling restores write. |
| `models/repo/repo_list_two_factor_test.go` | `AccessibleRepositoryCondition` and the separate "my repositories" branch drop the private repository, keep the public one, and return it after enrolment. |
| `tests/integration/org_two_factor_test.go` `TestOrgTwoFactorPolicy` (about 1.3s plus setup) | Before, blocked and after enrolment, for each path: **API** (repository, teams 403 with message, push permission, `/user/repos`, issue search); **git HTTP** (`info/refs`); **web** (repository, teams page, banner, no banner on the enrol page); **settings** (refused without 2FA, saved with it, counts, members and collaborators labels, unticking); **packages** (upload refused). |
| `tests/integration/org_two_factor_test.go` `TestOrgTwoFactorPolicySSH` | A blocked owner's SSH key is refused through the internal serv API. A deploy key on the same repository still pushes. |

LFS, the pre-receive hook and maintainer edits go through `GetIndividualUserRepoPermission`, which the permission unit tests cover. They have no separate end-to-end test.

## CI / manual verification

Locally, all passing:

```sh

go test -tags 'sqlite sqlite_unlock_notify' -run '^(TestAPINotification.*|TestNotification.*|TestAPIIssue.*|TestIssue.*|TestExplore.*|TestAPIRepo.*|TestUser.*|TestLFS.*|TestAPILFS.*|TestPackage.*|TestDashboard.*|TestMilestone.*|TestViewIssues.*|TestNoLoginViewIssues|TestAPIUserRepos.*|TestCodeSearch.*|TestSearch.*)$' gitea.dev/tests/integration
go test -run '^Test_AddRequireTwoFactorToUser$' ./models/migrations/v1_27/
make fmt, make lint-templates, golangci-lint on every changed package and tests/integration (0 issues), ./.claude-students/check.sh

Only SQLite was run locally. The new SQL uses only `builder` conditions (`IN`, `NOT IN`, `EXISTS`, bound booleans, quoted `` `user` ``), but MySQL, PostgreSQL and MSSQL are checked by CI only.

## Design

See Design Decisions 1–3 in #35. The implementation follows them. The one detail beyond the spec: the opt-out helper lives next to the check, as `organization.IgnoreTwoFactorPolicy`, so the organization-level guards honour it too.

Not fixed here, noticed on the way: the existing "Repository admin can add and remove access for teams" checkbox uses a `*bool` form field, which probably can't be unticked from the web form. That should go in a separate bug issue.

+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+package common
+
+import (
+	"testing"
+
+	"gitea.dev/models/db"
+	"gitea.dev/models/organization"
+	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
+	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
+	"gitea.dev/modules/session"
+	"gitea.dev/services/contexttest"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+func TestOrgTwoFactorRequired(t *testing.T) {
+	require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
+	org := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 3})
+	org.RequireTwoFactor = true
+	require.NoError(t, user_model.UpdateUserCols(t.Context(), org, "require_two_factor"))
+	for _, userID := range []int64{24, 32} {
+		require.NoError(t, db.Insert(t.Context(), &organization.OrgUser{OrgID: org.ID, UID: userID}))
+	}
+
+	for _, tc := range []struct {
+		name       string
+		userID     int64
+		session2FA bool
+		want       bool
+	}{
+		{"anonymous", 0, false, false},
+		{"member without 2FA", 4, false, true},
+		{"stale session flag", 4, true, true},
+		{"TOTP enrolled", 24, false, false},
+		{"WebAuthn enrolled", 32, false, false},
+		{"site admin", 1, false, false},
+		{"unrelated user", 5, false, false},
+	} {
+		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			store := session.NewMockMemStore(t.Name())
+			require.NoError(t, store.Set(session.KeyUserHasTwoFactorAuth, tc.session2FA))
+			ctx, _ := contexttest.MockContext(t, "/", contexttest.MockContextOption{SessionStore: store})
+			if tc.userID != 0 {
+				ctx.Doer = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: tc.userID})
+			}
+			assert.Equal(t, tc.want, orgTwoFactorRequired(ctx))
+		})
+	}
+}

I reviewed PR #76 (Jack-Donohue's org "require 2FA" feature, closes #35) and drafted the course-format review in [docs/sprint1/pr-76-review-draft.md](docs/sprint1/pr-76-review-draft.md). The rubric scores are all 7–9, and the overall verdict is to merge after three fixes. I worked from the diff and the PR description and haven't run the branch, apart from the CodeRabbit commit's tests below.

**Required fixes:**
- **R1 (most serious):** the new 2FA filter hides public-repo issues from users' dashboards (assigned, mentioned and created lists). Those lists only ever include public repos, which a blocked user can still read anyway. The filter doesn't check membership, so it also hits outside contributors who simply don't use 2FA: their own issues in a 2FA org's public repo vanish from their dashboard.
- **R2:** an owner can turn the policy on and then remove their own 2FA. That locks every owner out of the org's settings, and only a site admin can turn the policy off again.
- **R3:** the count of outside collaborators without 2FA still includes site admins, who are exempt from the policy. The member count already leaves them out.

There are also four optional points, mostly about query cost.

**CodeRabbit's autofix (commit `08864fd`) didn't break anything.** Its two new tests pass when I run them on the PR branch, and nothing else calls the changed code.
- **Leaving site admins out of the member count:** needed and correct, but only half done. The collaborator count still needs the same change (R3).
- **Removing the session-flag shortcut from the banner:** technically correct, but not really needed. The stale flag could only hide the warning banner, never grant access, because access checks always read the database. The cost is an extra database query on every page for every signed-in user with 2FA set up. The draft suggests either putting the shortcut back or adding a cheap "does any org require 2FA?" check first.

Before posting, fill in the TODO on the draft's "Checked" line by running the tests and trying R1 by hand. When the review is done, run `specstory sync`, file the log under `ai-logs/sprint1/<your-username>/`, and post your AI Assistance comment.

# AI assistance disclosure — required format

Course rule, not an upstream Gitea one. Every contributor discloses their own AI use per issue,
**even when no AI was used**. Source: the course AI Log Instructions page and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
(AI Contribution Policy). Two separate places, both required. The rest of the PR and issue
format is in `COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.

## 1. A comment on the issue

Posted by each contributor on the **issue** they worked, once their work is done. One comment per
person — never edit someone else's. Add later sessions by editing your own table.

```markdown
### AI Assistance — @your-github-username

**Role in this issue:** Implementation

| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-code | [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md) | Confirmed the files found during concept location, drafted the template change and tests, ran them |

**Attachments:** [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl/](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/tree/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl)
```

- **Role** is one of Implementation, Code review, Testing, Other — pick the ones that apply and
  delete the rest, do not leave the slash list in place.
- **Tool** is the tool's name, e.g. `claude-code`, `claude-web`.
- **Log** is a full `https://github.com/...` link to the filed log. Relative paths break in issue
  comments. File naming is in `ai-logs/README.md`.
- **Attachments** only when the log has a companion folder; otherwise drop the line.
- **No AI used?** Keep the heading and role line and write `No AI used` in place of the table.

## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link

Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, logs are
referenced in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page, D5).

code; I reviewed every line, ran the tests, checked the page by hand, and can explain each change.

```

Name the model, say what AI did and what you did, and point at the issue comment for the log.

## Rules that make a disclosure wrong

- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
  to the `main` link once merged.
- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the
  account is `Jack-Donohue`.
- **Claiming work AI did as your own, or the reverse.** The claim must match the log.
- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
  the questions are for you.

## For AI agents drafting an issue or PR

Put section 2 in every PR description you draft, and draft the section 1 issue comment
separately, both filled in from the session you actually ran — never with placeholders. You may
draft the wording, but say plainly that the human must review and edit it before posting, and leave
the issue comment for them to post under their own account.

# AI Logs

This folder holds every AI session for each sprint, one folder per student. The course rules are on
the [AI Log Instructions](https://csci-435-se.github.io/ai-logs/) page and the current sprint page
at <https://csci-435-se.github.io/>. This README is the team's shared convention for following them.

## What to log

Every AI session tied to this project: code, debugging, tests, reviews, drafting issues and PRs,
design discussion, the sprint report. That includes sessions that went nowhere. Purely academic
questions unrelated to the project don't need logging.

## Structure

```
ai-logs/
  sprint1/
    <github-username>/                          ← exact GitHub username, matching case
      .gitkeep                                  ← the folder must exist even if you used no AI
      YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md
      YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>/           ← attachments (images, etc.), optional
```

Team folders: `ab-wm`, `arjunsb26`, `CarsonRackley`, `controlled-opposition`, `Jack-Donohue`,
`vvchopra`.

## Naming

`YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`

- **Date:** the day the session started.
- **Sprint folder:** the sprint that date falls in, not the sprint the work is for.
- **Tool:** one of the course identifiers: `claude-code`, `claude-web`, `claude-desktop`, `cursor`,
  `gemini-cli`, `codex-cli`, `copilot`, `chatgpt`, `other-<name>`. Claude Code run inside VS Code is
  `claude-code`.
- **Slug:** lowercase words joined with hyphens that say what the session did. Put the issue number
  first when there is one: `issue-52-impl`, `issue-52-spec`, `pr-61-review`, `sprint1-report`.
  Replace auto-generated slugs such as `local-command-caveat...`.
- **Formats:** `.md` is preferred; `.txt` and `.json` are also accepted. No `.docx`, `.pdf`, `.html`
  or share links.

## Capturing a session

| Tool | How |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code (terminal or VS Code), other agentic CLIs | Start it with [SpecStory](https://specstory.com/): `specstory run claude`, from the repo root. Forgot? Run `specstory sync` afterwards; it back-fills from Claude Code's local history. Then copy from `.specstory/history/` (git-ignored) into your folder and rename it to the convention. |
| Web chat (claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini, ...) | Install a browser chat exporter and export the session as Markdown right after it ends. Include any files you pasted in as context. |
| Claude Desktop | SpecStory doesn't capture it. Copy the conversation into a `.md` file by hand. |

At the end of each sprint, run `specstory sync` once more and re-copy. A log copied mid-session is
incomplete.

## Content

- The **tool and AI model** used (SpecStory writes both).
- The **complete** prompt and response history. For agentic tools, that includes file edits and
  commands (SpecStory includes them). Logs with missing responses or truncated histories are
  **invalid**. Don't hand-write, summarise or trim a log; only rename it.
- Attachments (screenshots, snippets) go in a folder with the log's name minus `.md`.
- Log **every** session, including ones that went nowhere. Grading is on how complete the record
